name: Araunah
bio: Araunah was a Jebusite who owned a threshing floor in Jerusalem — the very spot where the angel of the LORD stopped striking Israel with plague after David, convicted over his sinful census, pleaded that the punishment fall on himself rather than the innocent people (2 Samuel 24:15-17). Told by the prophet Gad to build an altar there, David came to Araunah, who saw the king approaching and bowed to the ground before him. When David explained he had come to buy the threshing floor to build an altar and stop the plague, Araunah offered to give him everything he needed — the threshing floor, oxen for the sacrifice, and the threshing sledges for wood — free of charge, saying, "May the LORD your God accept you." David refused, insisting, "I will not sacrifice to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing," and bought the threshing floor and oxen for fifty shekels of silver. David built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and the LORD answered his prayer on behalf of the land, ending the plague (2 Samuel 24:18-25). This same threshing floor would later become the site of Solomon's temple, where Araunah is called by the name Ornan (2 Chronicles 3:1). In its own retelling of the purchase, 1 Chronicles 21:22-25 names the price as six hundred shekels of gold rather than fifty shekels of silver — likely reflecting a larger area of land beyond the threshing floor itself, bought for the temple complex as a whole. 2 Chronicles 3:1 also identifies the site as Mount Moriah, the same mountain where, centuries earlier, Abraham had been tested with the command to sacrifice Isaac (Genesis 22:2).
